exam.bokPreviousVersion: 2.0.1 (effective Feb 2025; restructured 7 domains -> 4). v1.0 (2023-24) had 7 domains.
bokChangesInV2_1: 'AI models' -> 'AI systems' terminology throughout (governance of the whole system, supply chain, downstream use)
Provider responsibilities made explicit; more emphasis on legal basis and transparency
Fundamental rights impact assessments; third-party AI risk management
I.C.2 modified: evaluate/update data governance AND intellectual property policies for AI
II.C expanded beyond EU AI Act to other enacted AI laws (e.g., South Korea AI Basic Act) - per secondary sources
II.D explicitly references ISO/IEC 42005 (AI system impact assessment)
Agentic architectures added as a deployment option example (Domain IV)

domains.name: Understanding the foundations of AI governance
subtopics: I.A Understand what AI is and why it needs governance (definitions, types of AI, risks & harms)
I.B Establish and communicate organizational expectations for AI governance (roles, cross-functional collaboration, training/AI literacy)

I.C Establish policies and procedures to apply throughout the AI life cycle (incl. updating privacy, security, data governance and IP policies; third-party) - heaviest Domain I competency (~6-8 Qs per a study site)

domains.name: Understanding how laws, standards and frameworks apply to AI
subtopics: II.A Understand how existing data privacy laws apply to AI (GDPR principles, lawful basis, ADM/Art 22, DPIA, data subject rights)
II.B Understand how other types of existing laws apply to AI (IP, anti-discrimination/employment, consumer protection/FTC, product liability)
II.C Understand the main elements of the EU AI Act (+ other enacted AI laws per v2.1)
II.D Understand the main industry standards and tools that apply to AI (OECD, NIST AI RMF, ISO/IEC 42001, 42005, 22989/23894 etc.)

domains.name: Understanding how to govern AI development
subtopics: III.A Govern the designing and building of the AI system (use-case, impact/risk assessment, requirements, documentation)
III.B Govern the collection and use of data in training and testing (data lineage, quality, bias, privacy, IP)
III.C Govern the release, monitoring and maintenance of the AI system (TEVV, red teaming, conformity, release readiness, post-market monitoring)

domains.name: Understanding how to govern AI deployment and use
subtopics: IV.A Evaluate key factors and risks relevant to the decision to deploy the AI system (context: business objectives, performance requirements, data availability, ethics, workforce readiness; deployment options incl. proprietary/open, cloud/on-prem, agentic)
IV.B Perform key activities to assess the AI system (impact assessments, vendor due diligence, contract terms)
IV.C Govern the deployment and use of the AI system (monitoring, incidents, secondary use, deactivation/decommissioning) - reportedly the heaviest competency

exam.domainSubtopicsCaveat: Competency names reconstructed from multiple secondary sources + v2.0.1 structure; the v2.1 PDF itself could not be opened from the sandbox. Verify against the PDF before building the plan.
exam.questionFormat: Multiple choice (mostly single answer; a candidate reported 2-3 multi-select items); ~30% tied to case-study scenarios (per third-party source)
exam.timeNotes: 2 h 45 min testing time plus an optional 15-min break at the midpoint (first half is submitted and locked) - ~3 h appointment. Some sources say '3 hours' (includes break). A LearnZapp claim of '90 questions in 2.5 hours' appears wrong.
exam.passingScore: 300 on a 100-500 scaled score (raw cut score converted; not 60%). No penalty for wrong answers - never leave blanks.
exam.feesVerified: Consistent across multiple third-party sources and the IAPP store search snippet; IAPP site itself could not be fetched.
exam.retakePolicy: Wait at least 7 days between attempts (per search snippet of store.iapp.org - verify in Candidate Handbook)
exam.membership: IAPP membership ~US$295/yr (saves $150 on exam; also covers certification maintenance) - unverified
exam.delivery: Pearson VUE test centre or OnVUE online proctoring
exam.passRate: Not published by IAPP. Third-party 'estimates' (45-55% first attempt) are unsourced marketing - ignore.
exam.euAiActCaveat: Digital Omnibus on AI in force 2026-07-27 deferred Annex III high-risk obligations to 2027-12-02 and Annex I to 2028-08-02. BoK v2.1 (approved Sep 2025) predates this - the exam item bank may still reflect original dates (Aug 2026/Aug 2027). Learn both.

readiness.hoursEvidenceQuality: LOW-MODERATE. No first-person report found that states total hours. Numbers are triangulated from: IAPP recommendation of >=30 h (reported secondhand by Privacy Bootcamp), vendor guides (40-60 h for privacy-cert holders with AI exposure; 80-120 h for newcomers; 60-120 h general), and one passer's '~2 months mostly after work'.
readiness.userAdjustedEstimate: ~50-65 h for this user (strong on frontier/policy context, weak on operational/legal detail): ~5 weeks at 12 h/week, with a buffer week.

hoursBeforeFirstPractice.diagnostic: ~3 h (after reading BoK v2.1 + IAPP free study guide questions; 15-25 free Qs)
hoursBeforeFirstPractice.notes: Take the first full-length (100-Q, timed) mock after ~25 h, i.e., after one full pass through all 4 domains.

practiceSchedule.what: Diagnostic: IAPP free-guide sample Qs + AIGP Playbook free preview (untimed)
Full mock #1 (timed 165 min) - third-party v2.1 bank
Re-take weakest-domain sets only; final review

targetPracticeScores.thirdPartyBanks: Consistently >=75% on two consecutive full mocks from a v2.1-aligned bank (common guidance across vendor sources); no domain below ~65-70%
targetPracticeScores.iappOfficialPracticeExam: >=70-75% under timed conditions (uncalibrated - IAPP publishes no mapping to the 300 cut score)
targetPracticeScores.bookingRule: Book when you hit the thresholds above AND can explain why each wrong option is wrong; many candidates book ~2-3 weeks ahead to fix a date.
targetPracticeScores.caveat: A vendor (Certsqill) publishes pass-rate-by-mock-score tables (e.g., 80%+ -> ~85% pass). These are unsourced; treat as marketing.

bluedotGapAnalysis.method: Inferred from BlueDot course unit descriptions (search snippets) vs BoK v2.1 competencies. BlueDot content itself not reviewed in depth.
strong: I.A AI types, capabilities, risks & harms (societal, frontier, misuse, catastrophic)
II.C GPAI / systemic-risk provisions of the EU AI Act and the GPAI Code of Practice (high level)
Policy landscape awareness: US federal stance, EU, UK, China, international treaties (CoE, OECD) at a high level
III.C concepts: evaluations, red-teaming, model/system cards
partial: I.B why organisations need AI governance, stakeholder mapping (BlueDot is state/lab-level, not enterprise)
II.D OECD principles (known), NIST AI RMF (probably known by name, not category-level)
weak: I.B/I.C enterprise program mechanics: governance committees, RACI, policies/procedures, AI inventories, training, third-party policies, IP policy updates
II.A GDPR applied to AI: lawful basis, purpose limitation, DPIA triggers, Art 22, data subject rights, EDPB Opinion 28/2024
II.B non-privacy law: copyright/IP, anti-discrimination (EEOC-type), consumer protection (FTC Section 5), product liability

II.C EU AI Act article-level detail for HIGH-RISK systems: Art 6 + Annex III classification, provider (Arts 9-17) vs deployer (Art 26) duties, Art 25 role shifts, FRIA (Art 27), Art 50 transparency, conformity assessment, penalties, timelines
II.D ISO/IEC 42001 (AIMS, Annex A), 42005, 23894; NIST AI RMF categories/subcategories
III.A-B lifecycle governance: use-case intake, impact assessments, data provenance/lineage, data quality & bias testing, documentation
IV.B vendor due diligence & contracts; IV.C monitoring, incident response, secondary use, decommissioning
US state/local laws: Colorado AI Act, NYC LL144, Texas TRAIGA; other national laws (Korea, Canada ADM directive, China GenAI measures, Singapore frameworks)
bluedotGapAnalysis.implication: Domains III and IV (~54% of scored items) plus II.A-II.C detail are where to spend ~70% of study time. Beware 'frontier-safety' answer instincts: AIGP rewards the process-correct, organisation-level governance action (document, assess, consult stakeholders, follow policy) rather than strategic/policy arguments.

practiceExams.reasoning: Only practice set written by IAPP-selected item writers; best signal for question style ('first', 'most appropriate'). Use it LAST as a calibration test (~1-2 weeks before exam). Small (100 Qs) and PDF format, so it cannot be your only bank. Confirm on the store page that it references BoK v2.1 before buying.

BUT no independent reviews found - evidence is vendor claims only. Use the FREE trial exam first; buy only if the free questions feel IAPP-like and you need more volume.

practiceExams.name: Braindump sites (ExamTopics, CertEmpire 'real exam questions', Pass4Success, ITExams, CertsHero, Study4Exam, P2PExams, CertShield, DumpsGate, etc.)

practiceExams.name: IAPP official AIGP training (online self-paced / live)
practiceExams.reasoning: Over budget. Not required: IAPP training is not a prerequisite.

prepCourseVerdict.reasoning: No recent (2025-26) evidence is strong enough to justify a paid course for someone with this background. The best-evidenced course (Dr. Kyle David's AIGP Masterclass) rests on one detailed first-person report (Veronica Lin, passed Jan 2026) plus platform ratings and vendor-hosted testimonials. The free stack (BoK v2.1, primary sources, IAPP glossary/tracker/Top-10 series, AIGP Playbook notes, Oliver Patel's guide, NIST playbook) covers the syllabus.

conditionalFallback.trigger: Full mock #1 (at ~25 h) below ~60% overall or below 55% in Domains III/IV
conditionalFallback.option: Kyle David 'AI Governance Professional (AIGP) Certification Masterclass' on Udemy (video-only version; ~4.7 stars, ~1.8k ratings per search snippet; buy during a Udemy sale; price unverified but Udemy sales are typically well under $150)
conditionalFallback.caveat: One search snippet described the Udemy version as covering BoK v2.0.1 (Mar 2025) with in-place updates promised; confirm the course page says v2.1 before buying. The practice questions/flashcards are only in the pricier own-site version (~EUR180).

alternative.option: AI Career Pro AIGP Exam Prep ($99; 5 mocks, v2.1-claimed)
alternative.caveat: No independent reviews; try the free Domain I-A + free practice exam first.

excluded: Privacy Bootcamp / Training Camp / InfosecTrain boot camps (prices not verified; almost certainly > $150)

revised.verdict: Recommend: AI Career Pro AIGP Exam Prep ($99)
revised.reason: Candidate needs a course to introduce and connect topics and to stay motivated; AI Career Pro is v2.1-mapped (vendor-stated), has 117 short video lessons with written and audio versions, 700+ questions and 5 mocks, has a free trial, and was already the plan's mock bank, so it costs nothing extra.
revised.caveat: No independent learner reviews found; use the Day-1 free trial as the check.
revised.alternative: Kyle David AIGP Masterclass (Udemy, 19-20 h; v2.1 status conflicting between listings; buy on sale)
